checklist: can the customer identify where to start?
can the first win actually be completed?
can the customer recover from common failure points?
does rescue route back into the mechanism?
does the product accidentally require unavailable information?
does it expose internal factory/governance terminology?
does the product actually deliver the specified mechanism rather than merely explain it?

rules.text: A first action and first win must be present and reachable.
Every asset referenced by the asset map must resolve and have authored source.
Failure points must be anticipated and carry a rescue route back into the mechanism.
No dead ends or circular instructions in the customer path.
No internal factory/governance terminology exposed to the customer.
The product must deliver the specified mechanism (not merely explain it).
The next state must be understandable (maintenance / next transformation).

aggregation_policy: A deterministic failure always blocks. Model simulation roles may only ADD findings; no single model may override a constitutional requirement. AUTHORIZED requires: all deterministic checks pass AND no blocking model finding.
automatic_authorization_conditions: first action + first win present and reachable
all assets resolve with authored source
failure points rescue back into the mechanism
no deterministic dead end / missing transition

provenance.note: The 20-question checklist is reused verbatim from the existing journey review. Deterministic checks replace the mandatory human walk-through for normal products; simulation roles derive from canonical Customer Truth, never fabricated personas.
